name: Technical manuals
description: Stations, components, actuators, sensors, I/O signals and operation sequences from plant and machine documentation.
purpose: Extract a mechatronic plant model from technical manuals and design documents, covering what each station is made of, how its components are wired by signal, and in which order its operations run.
scope: In scope: stations, components (actuators and sensors), I/O signals, operations and motions with their sequence and duration, and component attributes such as part number, position and operating pressure. Out of scope: control-program logic, electrical schematics at wire level, and maintenance schedules.
stories: As an automation engineer I want each component linked to its station and its I/O signals so that I can check the I/O list against the documentation.
As a commissioning engineer I want the sequence of operations, the components they act on and their durations so that I can verify cycle timing.
As a maintenance planner I want part numbers and operating pressures for every component so that I can order spares and set up the pneumatics correctly.
cqs: Which components belong to each station?
Which components of a station are actuators and which are sensors?
Which signals does each component emit or receive, and what is each signal's I/O type?
Which component does each operation or motion act on?
Which operation precedes which in a station's sequence of operation?
How long does each operation take, in seconds?
What is the operating pressure, in kPa, of each pneumatic component?
What is the manufacturer part number of each component?
Which named or numeric positions can each component take?
